_comment: Maps the ~20 PDF look-book categories to their predictions-dataset product_type(s). Only categories that appear in the PDF need an entry here — every other predictions product_type (the other ~165) simply has no PDF price/day coverage and falls back to predictions pricing + a carryover-default Friday day. title_prefix (optional) further restricts a product_type match to titles starting with that string, for cases where one product_type covers two different PDF categories (e.g. 'Underwear' covers both Boy's Briefs and Girl's Undies).
pdf_category_aliases_comment: Some PDF pages phrase the same product line's category header slightly differently (e.g. 'Toddler Short Sleeve with Pants Pajamas' on one page vs '...Pajama Set' on another) — maps the normalized variant text to the normalized canonical text so both resolve to one category instead of splitting into two, one of which would otherwise be an orphaned PDF-only category with no real product data to draw sizes from.

pdf_category_aliases.toddler short sleeve with pants pajamas: toddler short sleeve with pants pajama set

manual_price_overrides_comment: Keyed by Kyte's raw product_type. Only applied when the pipeline found zero sale-price evidence anywhere (predictions price_confidence == 'no_baseline_match' AND no PDF/look-book coverage) — fills in the user's own memory of a past sale's price for that product. Never overrides a real PDF-confirmed price.
excluded_prints_comment: Prints confirmed (e.g. via Kyte's Instagram Live) to NOT actually be in the sale, despite Look Book/historical-snapshot evidence suggesting otherwise. Filtered out everywhere — real products, PDF-only entries, historical backfill — before entries are built.
category_renames_comment: Kyte's own raw product_type occasionally uses two different names for what is really one product line. Renames the display category (and its normalized id) to the canonical name after category resolution, so both sides merge into one entry instead of splitting into an orphaned duplicate.
category_price_overrides_comment: Keyed by the exact category display name. Overrides EVERY print's price in that category to a flat confirmed number, regardless of what price source the pipeline otherwise derived (predictions, PDF, sibling-inferred) — used when Kyte confirmed a flat promotional price for a whole product line (e.g. via Instagram Live).
manual_print_additions_comment: Prints confirmed (e.g. via Instagram Live) for specific categories that neither the Look Book PDF text nor a historical snapshot already covers. Added as pdf-only entries (no real live product), so sizes/price are inferred from sibling prints in the same category exactly like any other PDF-only print. Automatically skipped if the (category, print) pair is already covered by a real product or another loop, so it's safe to list a category that might already have this print.
